source.text: אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב יִשְׁנֶ֖א הַכֶּ֣תֶם הַטּ֑וֹב תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֨כְנָה֙ אַבְנֵי־קֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּרֹ֖אשׁ כָּל־חוּצֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: How! is dimmed gold, is changed the gold the pure; are poured out stones of holiness at [the] head of all streets.

en.L: How the gold has grown dim, the pure gold changed! \q Stones of holiness are poured out at the head of every street.
en.B: How the gold has lost its shine, the finest gold has changed! \q The sacred stones lie scattered at the corner of every street.
en.R: How the gold has lost its shine! The finest gold has changed. \q The holy stones lie scattered on every street corner.

fr.L: Comme l’or s’est terni, l’or pur s’est altéré ! \q Les pierres de sainteté sont répandues au coin de toutes les rues.
fr.B: Comme l’or a perdu son éclat, comme l’or le plus fin s’est altéré ! \q Les pierres sacrées gisent dispersées au coin de chaque rue.
fr.R: Comme l’or a perdu son éclat ! L’or le plus pur a changé. \q Les pierres saintes traînent au coin de chaque rue.

decisions.choice: an alphabet poem: twenty-two verses, one for each letter
decisions.reason: Like chapters 1 and 2, this chapter is an acrostic: each of its twenty-two verses begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, from aleph here to taw in verse 22. Its verses are shorter than those of chapters 1-3, two lines each instead of three, and most lines have the uneven lament rhythm, a longer half followed by a shorter one, explained at 1:1. As in 2:16-17 and 3:46-51, the letter pe comes before ayin (verses 16-17; see the note at 2:1).

decisions.choice: How ...!: a cry of grief and shock, and the book's Hebrew title
decisions.reason: The word ('ekhah) is an exclamation, not a question: the cry of a mourner over the dead (compare Isaiah 1:21; Jeremiah 48:17), here over a fallen city. It opens chapters 1, 2 and 4, and it is the Hebrew name of the book.

decisions.choice: the gold and the holy stones: Zion's precious people
alternatives: the gold of the temple and the stones of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Verse 2 explains the picture: the people of Zion, once worth their weight in gold, are now treated like cheap pots. So the dimmed gold and the stones lying in the streets most likely stand for the people, lying in the streets like the fainting children of 2:19, where the same phrase "at the head of every street" is used. The words could also be taken at face value, of the temple's gold and the stones of the sanctuary scattered when it was burned (2 Kings 25:9, 13-17).

decisions.choice: at the head of every street: at every street corner
decisions.reason: The "head" of a street is where it begins, at a corner or crossing, the most public place (2:19; Isaiah 51:20).

decisions.choice: lie scattered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "lie scattered" for the verb "are poured out", since stones are not poured.

decisions.choice: How ...!
decisions.reason: As at 1:1, every level keeps "How" with an exclamation mark (m2).

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י צִיּוֹן֙ הַיְקָרִ֔ים הַמְסֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑ז אֵיכָ֤ה נֶחְשְׁבוּ֙ לְנִבְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶשׂ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י יוֹצֵֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Zion, the precious, the [ones] weighed against fine gold, how! they are reckoned as jars of earthenware, [the] work of [the] hands of a potter.

en.L: The precious {{gender:children|sons}} of Zion, weighed against fine gold, \q how they are reckoned as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands!
en.B: Zion's precious {{gender:children|sons}}, once worth their weight in fine gold, \q how they are now counted as common clay pots, the work of a potter's hands!
en.R: The people of Zion were precious, worth as much as pure gold. \q But now they are treated like cheap clay pots that a potter makes.

fr.L: Les précieux {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Sion, pesés contre l’or fin, \q comme ils sont comptés pour des cruches d’argile, l’ouvrage des mains d’un potier !
fr.B: Les précieux {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Sion, qui valaient autrefois leur poids d’or fin, \q comme ils sont maintenant considérés comme de vulgaires pots d’argile, l’ouvrage des mains d’un potier !
fr.R: Les gens de Sion étaient précieux, ils valaient autant que l’or pur. \q Mais maintenant on les traite comme des pots d’argile bon marché, fabriqués par un potier.

decisions.choice: the sons of Zion: the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "Sons of Zion" means Zion's people, men and women alike, as "sons of Israel" means Israelites.

decisions.choice: weighed against fine gold: valued as highly as gold
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it means to weigh or value one thing against another (Job 28:16, 19, where wisdom cannot be valued in gold). Zion's people were worth their weight in the finest gold.

decisions.choice: clay jars, the work of a potter: cheap, easily broken and thrown away
decisions.reason: Clay pots were common and cheap; a broken one was thrown away (Jeremiah 19:10-11; Isaiah 30:14). The people once valued like gold are now treated as worthless.

decisions.choice: once ... now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "once" and "now" to make the contrast of the verse plain.

source.text: גַּם־תַּנִּים֙ חָ֣לְצוּ שַׁ֔ד הֵינִ֖יקוּ גּוּרֵיהֶ֑ן בַּת־עַמִּ֣י לְאַכְזָ֔ר כַּיְעֵנִ֖ים בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Even jackals draw out [the] breast, they nurse their young; [the] daughter of my people [has become] cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.

en.L: Even jackals offer the breast; they nurse their young. \q The daughter of my people [has become] cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.
en.B: Even jackals offer the breast and nurse their young, \q but my dear people have become cruel, like ostriches in the desert.
en.R: Even wild jackals feed their young with their own milk. \q But my people have become cruel, like ostriches in the desert that do not care for their young.

fr.L: Même les chacals présentent la mamelle, ils allaitent leurs petits ; \q la fille de mon peuple [est devenue] cruelle, comme les autruches dans le désert.
fr.B: Même les chacals tendent la mamelle et allaitent leurs petits, \q mais mon cher peuple est devenu cruel, comme les autruches du désert.
fr.R: Même les chacals sauvages nourrissent leurs petits de leur lait. \q Mais mon peuple est devenu cruel, comme les autruches du désert, qui ne s’occupent pas de leurs petits.

decisions.choice: jackals ... like ostriches, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: In two places the reading the scribes marked (qere) differs from the written consonants (ketiv). The written form of "jackals" has an ending that could be read as "sea monsters" or "serpents" (tannin), but the nursing animals of the desert are jackals. And the written consonants divide "like ostriches" into two words ("for ostriches"). The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: ostriches: birds thought to neglect their young
decisions.reason: The ostrich lays its eggs in the sand and was thought to leave them and treat its young harshly (Job 39:13-16). Even jackals, scavengers of the ruins, feed their young; Zion's mothers no longer can (verses 4 and 10).

decisions.choice: the daughter of my people: my people, dear as a daughter
decisions.reason: The phrase names the people of Jerusalem as one beloved young woman, as "daughter Zion" does (verse 22). The poet speaks of them with grief and love. It returns in verses 6 and 10.

decisions.choice: my dear people (B); my people (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the daughter of my people". Balanced says "my dear people" to keep the tenderness of the phrase; Readable says "my people". The same wording is used in verses 6 and 10.

decisions.choice: that do not care for their young
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the ostrich is named.

source.text: דָּבַ֨ק לְשׁ֥וֹן יוֹנֵ֛ק אֶל־חכּ֖וֹבַּצָּמָ֑א עֽוֹלָלִים֙ שָׁ֣אֲלוּ לֶ֔חֶם פֹּרֵ֖שׂ אֵ֥ין לָהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Cleaves [the] tongue of [the] nursing [child] to its palate in thirst; children ask [for] bread; [one] breaking [it] is not for them.

en.L: The tongue of the nursing child clings to its palate for thirst; \q little children ask for bread; there is no one breaking [it] for them.
en.B: The nursing baby's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth from thirst; \q little children beg for bread, but no one shares any with them.
en.R: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths. \q Little children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.

fr.L: La langue du nourrisson colle à son palais à cause de la soif ; \q les petits enfants demandent du pain ; il n’y a personne qui [le] leur rompe.
fr.B: La langue du bébé qui tète colle à son palais tant il a soif ; \q les petits enfants réclament du pain, mais personne ne le partage avec eux.
fr.R: Les bébés ont tellement soif que leur langue colle à leur palais. \q Les petits enfants demandent du pain, mais personne ne leur en donne.

decisions.choice: no one breaking it for them: no one gives them food
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in flat loaves that were broken by hand to be shared out (Isaiah 58:7; Jeremiah 16:7). No one has any bread to break for the children.

decisions.choice: children: little children, past nursing
decisions.reason: The word ('olalim) means small children (2:11, 19). The verse moves from babies at the breast, who have no milk, to young children, who have no bread.

decisions.choice: the roof of its mouth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday phrase for "palate".

source.text: הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ לְמַ֣עֲדַנִּ֔ים נָשַׁ֖מּוּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת הָאֱמֻנִים֙ עֲלֵ֣י תוֹלָ֔ע חִבְּק֖וּ אַשְׁפַּתּֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Those eating delicacies are desolate in [the] streets; those brought up on crimson embrace ash heaps.

en.L: Those who ate delicacies are desolate in the streets; \q those brought up in crimson embrace ash heaps.
en.B: Those who once ate fine food lie ruined in the streets; \q those raised in scarlet clothing now cling to the garbage heaps.
en.R: People who used to eat the best food now lie starving in the streets. \q Those who grew up wearing fine red clothes now lie on piles of garbage.

fr.L: Ceux qui mangeaient des mets délicats sont désolés dans les rues ; \q ceux qui étaient élevés dans l’écarlate embrassent les tas d’ordures.
fr.B: Ceux qui mangeaient autrefois des mets fins gisent, ruinés, dans les rues ; \q ceux qui ont grandi vêtus d’écarlate s’accrochent maintenant aux tas d’ordures.
fr.R: Les gens qui mangeaient la meilleure nourriture meurent maintenant de faim dans les rues. \q Ceux qui ont grandi en portant de beaux habits rouges sont couchés sur des tas d’ordures.

decisions.choice: are desolate: ruined and dying
decisions.reason: The verb means to be laid waste, stunned or destitute. Used of people in the streets during a famine, it means they lie ruined and perishing.

decisions.choice: crimson: costly clothing of the rich
decisions.reason: Crimson dye was made from an insect and was costly; clothing dyed with it was worn by the wealthy (2 Samuel 1:24; Jeremiah 4:30). The people meant are those raised in luxury.

decisions.choice: embrace ash heaps: lie on the refuse dumps
decisions.reason: The ash heap was the dump outside a town where ashes and refuse were thrown, where the poorest sat and begged (1 Samuel 2:8; Psalm 113:7). To "embrace" it is to cling to it or lie on it, perhaps searching it for food.

decisions.choice: cling to the garbage heaps (B); lie on piles of garbage (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the ash heaps as garbage dumps, which is what they were.

source.text: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ עֲוֺ֣ן בַּת־עַמִּ֔י מֵֽחַטַּ֖את סְדֹ֑ם הַֽהֲפוּכָ֣ה כְמוֹ־רָ֔גַע וְלֹא־חָ֥לוּ בָ֖הּ יָדָֽיִם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And is greater [the] iniquity of [the] daughter of my people than [the] sin of Sodom, the [one] overthrown as [in] a moment, and not whirled on her hands.

en.L: And the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, \q which was overthrown as in a moment, and no hands whirled upon her.
en.B: The punishment of my dear people is greater than the penalty for Sodom's sin; \q Sodom was overthrown in an instant, and no human hands were raised against her.
en.R: My people have been punished more than Sodom was punished for its sin. \q Sodom was destroyed in a moment, and no human hand was raised against it.

fr.L: Et la faute de la fille de mon peuple est plus grande que le péché de Sodome, \q qui a été renversée comme en un instant, et aucune main ne s’est agitée contre elle.
fr.B: La punition de mon cher peuple est plus grande que la peine du péché de Sodome ; \q Sodome a été renversée en un instant, sans qu’aucune main humaine se lève contre elle.
fr.R: Mon peuple a été puni plus durement que Sodome n’a été punie pour son péché. \q Sodome a été détruite en un moment, sans qu’aucune main humaine l’attaque.

decisions.choice: iniquity ... sin: the punishment that iniquity brings
alternatives: the sin of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom
decisions.reason: The two words ('awon, chatta't) can mean a wrong or the penalty it brings. The rest of the verse compares what happened to the two cities, so the point is most likely the punishment: Sodom's ended in a moment, while Jerusalem's drags on through siege and famine. The words can also be read as the guilt itself: Jerusalem's sin is worse than Sodom's (Ezekiel 16:46-50). In 4:22 the first word plainly means punishment.

decisions.choice: Sodom, overthrown in a moment
decisions.reason: God overthrew Sodom with fire from heaven (Genesis 19:24-25); the same verb "overthrow" is used there. Sodom is the standing example of sudden, complete judgment (Deuteronomy 29:22; Isaiah 1:9-10; Jeremiah 49:18).

decisions.choice: no hands whirled upon her: no human attackers worked her downfall
alternatives: no hands were wrung over her
decisions.reason: The sense of the verb here is unclear; it may mean that no hands were turned or laid on Sodom. Most likely the point is that no army besieged it: God destroyed it at once, without the long suffering of a siege. It may instead mean that no hands were wrung in long anguish over it.

decisions.choice: no human hands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "human" to make the point of m3 clear.

decisions.choice: punishment (B); punished (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in m1, the punishment, instead of the usual "guilt" and "sin" for this word ('awon, as in verse 13 and 5:7); Literal keeps "iniquity", which can carry either sense. Verse 22 does the same for Zion.

source.text: זַכּ֤וּ נְזִירֶ֨יהָ֙ מִשֶּׁ֔לֶג צַח֖וּ מֵחָלָ֑ב אָ֤דְמוּ עֶ֨צֶם֙ מִפְּנִינִ֔ים סַפִּ֖יר גִּזְרָתָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Were purer her princes than snow, were whiter than milk; were ruddier [in] body than corals, sapphire [was] their form.

en.L: Her princes were purer than snow, whiter than milk; \q they were ruddier in body than corals; their form [was] sapphire.
en.B: Her princes were brighter than snow and whiter than milk; \q their bodies glowed redder than coral; they had the beauty of lapis lazuli.
en.R: Zion's princes were once cleaner than snow and whiter than milk. \q Their bodies glowed red like coral, and they shone like precious blue stones.

fr.L: Ses princes étaient plus purs que la neige, plus blancs que le lait ; \q ils étaient plus vermeils de corps que les coraux ; leur forme [était] saphir.
fr.B: Ses princes étaient plus éclatants que la neige et plus blancs que le lait ; \q leur corps était plus vermeil que le corail ; ils avaient la beauté du lapis-lazuli.
fr.R: Autrefois, les princes de Sion étaient plus propres que la neige et plus blancs que le lait. \q Leur corps avait l’éclat rouge du corail, et ils brillaient comme des pierres précieuses bleues.

decisions.choice: her princes: Zion's nobles
decisions.reason: The word (nazir) means one who is set apart. It usually names a Nazirite, a person under a vow (Numbers 6:2), but it is also used of a prince set apart from his brothers (Genesis 49:26; Deuteronomy 33:16). Here the beauty and health described, set against the famine of verse 8, fit the young nobles of the city best. The verse may instead speak of Nazirites, whose vow kept them from wine and made them pure.

decisions.choice: purer, whiter, ruddier: radiant with health
decisions.reason: The words picture shining skin and healthy color, as David was "ruddy" and handsome (1 Samuel 16:12; Song 5:10). Verse 8 reverses each picture.

decisions.choice: coral ... sapphire: costly red and blue stones
decisions.reason: The first word (peninim) names a precious red stone, most likely coral (Job 28:18; Proverbs 3:15). Sappir is the deep blue stone of Exodus 24:10, probably lapis lazuli rather than the modern sapphire. The last word (gizrah) may mean their form or the cut and polish of a stone.

decisions.choice: lapis lazuli
decisions.reason: Balanced names the stone the word most likely means; Literal keeps the traditional "sapphire" and Readable says "precious blue stones".

decisions.choice: once
decisions.reason: Readable adds "once" to show the contrast with verse 8.

decisions.choice: princes
decisions.reason: Every level says "princes" here, although Numbers says "Nazirite" for this word at every level. In Numbers the word names a person under the vow of Numbers 6; here it is taken in its wider sense of one set apart, as of Joseph in Genesis 49:26 and Deuteronomy 33:16, because the beauty and health described, set against verse 8, fit the city's nobles best (m1). The reading "Nazirites" is footnoted with m1.

source.text: חָשַׁ֤ךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר֙ תָּֽאֳרָ֔ם לֹ֥א נִכְּר֖וּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת צָפַ֤ד עוֹרָם֙ עַל־עַצְמָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה כָעֵֽץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Is darker than blackness their appearance; not are they recognized in [the] streets; has shriveled their skin on their bones; dry it has become like wood.

en.L: Their appearance is darker than blackness; they are not recognized in the streets; \q their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become dry as wood.
en.B: Now they look blacker than soot; no one knows them in the streets. \q Their skin has shrunk onto their bones; it has become as dry as a stick.
en.R: Now their faces are blacker than soot, and no one in the streets knows who they are. \q Their skin has shriveled on their bones and become as dry as wood.

fr.L: Leur aspect est plus sombre que la noirceur ; on ne les reconnaît pas dans les rues ; \q leur peau s’est ratatinée sur leurs os ; elle est devenue sèche comme du bois.
fr.B: Maintenant, ils ont l’air plus noirs que la suie ; personne ne les reconnaît dans les rues. \q Leur peau s’est collée à leurs os ; elle est devenue sèche comme un bâton.
fr.R: Maintenant, leur visage est plus noir que la suie, et dans les rues personne ne sait qui ils sont. \q Leur peau s’est ratatinée sur leurs os et elle est devenue sèche comme du bois.

decisions.choice: darker than blackness, skin dried like wood: the marks of starvation
decisions.reason: Long hunger darkens and blackens the skin and shrinks it onto the bones (5:10; Job 30:30; Psalm 102:6). The radiant nobles of verse 7 can no longer be recognized.

decisions.choice: blackness: soot
decisions.reason: The word (shechor) occurs only here; it comes from the root for "black" and probably means soot.

decisions.choice: Now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "now" to mark the turn from verse 7.

source.text: טוֹבִ֤ים הָיוּ֙ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵֽחַלְלֵ֖י רָעָ֑ב שֶׁ֣הֵ֤ם יָז֨וּבוּ֙ מְדֻקָּרִ֔ים מִתְּנוּבֹ֖ת שָׂדָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Better were [the] slain of [the] sword than [the] slain of hunger, who waste away, pierced, from [the] produce of [the] field.

en.L: Better off were those slain by the sword than those slain by hunger, \q who waste away, pierced through, for lack of the produce of the field.
en.B: Those killed by the sword were better off than those killed by hunger, \q who waste away as if stabbed, for want of food from the fields.
en.R: It was better to be killed in battle than to die of hunger. \q The starving waste away slowly, as if they had been stabbed, because there is no food from the fields.

fr.L: Plus heureux ont été les tués par l’épée que les tués par la faim, \q qui dépérissent, transpercés, faute des produits des champs.
fr.B: Ceux que l’épée a tués ont eu un meilleur sort que ceux que la faim a tués, \q qui dépérissent comme s’ils étaient transpercés, faute de nourriture venant des champs.
fr.R: Il valait mieux être tué au combat que mourir de faim. \q Ceux qui ont faim dépérissent lentement, comme s’ils avaient été poignardés, parce que les champs ne donnent plus de nourriture.

decisions.choice: who waste away, pierced through: the starving, wounded by hunger
alternatives: the slain of the sword, who bleed away, pierced through
decisions.reason: The "who" most likely refers to those slain by hunger: they waste away as surely as if they had been run through, while the sword kills quickly. It could also describe the sword's victims, who bleed away quickly, set against those who die slowly for lack of food.

decisions.choice: from the produce of the field: for lack of its crops
decisions.reason: The word "from" here means "away from", that is, deprived of. During the siege no crops could come in from the fields outside the walls (2 Kings 25:3).

source.text: יְדֵ֗י נָשִׁים֙ רַחֲמָ֣נִיּ֔וֹת בִּשְּׁל֖וּ יַלְדֵיהֶ֑ן הָי֤וּ לְבָרוֹת֙ לָ֔מוֹ בְּשֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] hands of compassionate women have boiled their children; they became food for them in [the] destruction of [the] daughter of my people.

en.L: The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; \q they became food for them in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
en.B: With their own hands, tender-hearted women have cooked their children; \q they became their food when my dear people were shattered.
en.R: Women who were once kind and loving mothers cooked their own children. \q They ate them when my people were destroyed.

fr.L: Les mains de femmes compatissantes ont fait bouillir leurs propres enfants ; \q ils sont devenus leur nourriture dans le désastre de la fille de mon peuple.
fr.B: De leurs propres mains, des femmes au cœur tendre ont fait cuire leurs enfants ; \q ils sont devenus leur nourriture quand mon cher peuple a été brisé.
fr.R: Des femmes qui étaient autrefois des mères douces et aimantes ont fait cuire leurs propres enfants. \q Elles les ont mangés quand mon peuple a été détruit.

decisions.choice: women boiled their children: the curse of the siege fulfilled
decisions.reason: The law warned that in a siege parents would eat their own children if the people broke the covenant (Leviticus 26:29; Deuteronomy 28:53-57), and Jeremiah repeated the warning (Jeremiah 19:9). It had happened in the siege of Samaria (2 Kings 6:28-29). Lamentations 2:20 has already named it.

decisions.choice: compassionate: loving by nature
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root for a mother's womb and her tender love (Isaiah 49:15). The famine has driven even such women to this.

decisions.choice: destruction: the breaking of the city
decisions.reason: The word (shever) means a breaking or crushing; here it is the fall of Jerusalem (2:11; 3:48).

decisions.choice: They ate them
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "they became food for them" means.

source.text: כִּלָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־חֲמָת֔וֹ שָׁפַ֖ךְ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּצֶּת־אֵ֣שׁ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וַתֹּ֖אכַל יְסוֹדֹתֶֽיהָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Has completed Yahweh his rage; he has poured out [the] burning of his anger, and he kindled a fire in Zion, and it consumed her foundations.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has completed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rage; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has carried {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury through to the end; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger. \q He lit a fire in Zion, and it devoured her to her foundations.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has let all of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger loose. He poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger. \q He started a fire in Zion that burned it down to its foundations.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a épuisé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a répandu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ardente, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a allumé un feu dans Sion, et il a dévoré ses fondations.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a mené {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur jusqu’au bout ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a répandu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère brûlante. \q Il a allumé un feu dans Sion, et ce feu l’a dévorée jusqu’à ses fondations.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a laissé éclater toute {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère. Il a déversé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère brûlante. \q Il a allumé dans Sion un feu qui l’a brûlée jusqu’à ses fondations.

decisions.choice: has completed his rage: has let his anger run its full course
decisions.reason: The verb (killah) means to finish or bring to an end. The LORD has not held back any part of his anger; he has carried it out fully (Ezekiel 5:13; 7:8).

decisions.choice: he kindled a fire in Zion: the burning of Jerusalem as the LORD's act
decisions.reason: The Babylonians burned the temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9). The poem sees the hand of the LORD in it, as the prophets had warned (Jeremiah 17:27; 21:10; Amos 2:5). The fire burning to the foundations echoes Deuteronomy 32:22.

source.text: לֹ֤א הֶאֱמִ֨ינוּ֙ מַלְכֵי־אֶ֔רֶץ כֹּ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל כִּ֤י יָבֹא֙ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not believed [the] kings of [the] earth, and all [the] inhabitants of [the] world, that would enter foe and enemy into [the] gates of Jerusalem.

en.L: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor all the inhabitants of the world, \q that foe and enemy would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
en.B: The kings of the earth would not have believed it, nor would anyone living in the world, \q that an enemy or attacker could march in through the gates of Jerusalem.
en.R: No king on earth, and no one anywhere in the world, believed \q that an enemy could ever march in through the gates of Jerusalem.

fr.L: Les rois de la terre n’ont pas cru, ni tous les habitants du monde, \q que l’adversaire et l’ennemi entreraient par les portes de Jérusalem.
fr.B: Les rois de la terre ne l’auraient pas cru, ni aucun des habitants du monde, \q qu’un adversaire, un ennemi, puisse franchir les portes de Jérusalem.
fr.R: Aucun roi de la terre, et personne dans le monde entier, ne croyait \q qu’un ennemi pourrait un jour entrer par les portes de Jérusalem.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: Jerusalem was thought unconquerable
decisions.reason: Jerusalem had stood for centuries and had been spared when the Assyrians surrounded it (2 Kings 19:32-36). Songs of Zion praised it as the city God would never let fall (Psalm 46:6; 48:5-9), and the people trusted that the temple would keep them safe (Jeremiah 7:4). Its fall seemed impossible.

decisions.choice: all the inhabitants, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) differ slightly at the word "all"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: would not have believed it
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the kings would have thought before it happened.

source.text: מֵֽחַטֹּ֣את נְבִיאֶ֔יהָ עֲוֺנ֖וֹת כֹּהֲנֶ֑יהָ הַשֹּׁפְכִ֥ים בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ דַּ֥ם צַדִּיקִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Because of [the] sins of her prophets, [the] iniquities of her priests, who shed in her midst [the] blood of righteous [people].

en.L: [It was] because of the sins of her prophets, the iniquities of her priests, \q who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
en.B: It was for the sins of her prophets and her priests' guilt, \q since they spilled the blood of the righteous in the midst of the city.
en.R: This happened because her prophets sinned and her priests did wrong. \q They killed innocent people inside the city.

fr.L: [C’est] à cause des péchés de ses prophètes, des fautes de ses prêtres, \q qui ont versé au milieu d’elle le sang des justes.
fr.B: C’est à cause des péchés de ses prophètes et de la culpabilité de ses prêtres, \q car ils ont versé le sang des justes au milieu de la ville.
fr.R: Cela est arrivé parce que ses prophètes ont péché et que ses prêtres ont fait le mal. \q Ils ont tué des innocents dans la ville.

decisions.choice: because of the sins: the reason Jerusalem fell
decisions.reason: The verse has no main verb of its own. It gives the cause of what verses 11-12 describe: the enemy entered Jerusalem because of the sins of its religious leaders.

decisions.choice: her prophets ... her priests: Jerusalem's religious leaders
decisions.reason: Jeremiah accused the prophets and priests of Jerusalem of lies and godlessness (Jeremiah 6:13-14; 23:11), and they demanded his death (Jeremiah 26:7-11). The prophet Uriah was put to death by the king (Jeremiah 26:20-23).

decisions.choice: shed the blood of the righteous: killed innocent people
decisions.reason: The righteous are those in the right, the innocent (Jeremiah 2:34; 7:6; 22:3). Shedding innocent blood was one of the sins that brought the city's fall (2 Kings 24:4).

decisions.choice: guilt (B); did wrong (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, 'awon is "iniquity" at Literal, "guilt" at Balanced and a plain word for sin at Readable.

decisions.choice: It was for (B); This happened because (R)
decisions.reason: The verse gives a reason without a main verb; Balanced and Readable supply a short clause to link it to verses 11-12. Literal puts the same words in brackets.

source.text: נָע֤וּ עִוְרִים֙ בַּֽחוּצ֔וֹת נְגֹֽאֲל֖וּ בַּדָּ֑ם בְּלֹ֣א יֽוּכְל֔וּ יִגְּע֖וּ בִּלְבֻשֵׁיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They wandered [as] blind [people] in [the] streets; they were defiled with blood, so that not were able [people that] they touch their garments.

en.L: They wandered blind through the streets; they were defiled with blood, \q so that [no one] was able to touch their garments.
en.B: They staggered blind through the streets, so defiled with blood \q that no one could touch their clothes.
en.R: They stumbled through the streets like blind men. They were so stained with blood \q that no one could touch their clothes.

fr.L: Ils ont erré, aveugles, dans les rues ; ils étaient souillés de sang, \q si bien que [personne] ne pouvait toucher leurs vêtements.
fr.B: Ils ont titubé, aveugles, dans les rues, si souillés de sang \q que personne ne pouvait toucher leurs vêtements.
fr.R: Ils ont marché en trébuchant dans les rues, comme des aveugles. Ils étaient tellement tachés de sang \q que personne ne pouvait toucher leurs vêtements.

decisions.choice: they: the prophets and priests of verse 13
decisions.reason: The subject is most likely the prophets and priests just named, stained with the blood they shed. It could be the people of the city in general, wandering dazed among the dead.

decisions.choice: defiled with blood, no one could touch their clothes: ritually unclean
decisions.reason: Blood and contact with the dead made a person unclean, and anyone who touched them or their clothes became unclean too (Numbers 19:11-22; Leviticus 15:4-12). The priests, who were to keep themselves pure, have become untouchable.

decisions.choice: blind: groping, without direction
decisions.reason: They move like blind people, unable to see where they go (Deuteronomy 28:28-29; Isaiah 59:10). It is a picture of their confusion, not of loss of sight.

decisions.choice: like blind men
decisions.reason: Readable says "like" to show this is a picture; "men" because the prophets and priests were men.

source.text: ס֣וּרוּ טָמֵ֞א קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֗מוֹ ס֤וּרוּ ס֨וּרוּ֙ אַל־תִּגָּ֔עוּ כִּ֥י נָצ֖וּ גַּם־נָ֑עוּ אָֽמְרוּ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יפוּ לָגֽוּר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Turn away! Unclean! they called to them; Turn away! Turn away! Do not touch! For they fled, also they wandered; they said among the nations, Not they will continue to sojourn.

en.L: "Turn away! Unclean!" they called to them; "Turn away! Turn away! Do not touch!" \q For they fled and also wandered; \q they said among the nations, "They will not continue to sojourn [here]."
en.B: "Go away! Unclean!" people shouted at them. "Go away! Go away! Do not touch us!" \q So they fled and wandered from place to place, \q and among the nations people said, "They cannot stay here any longer."
en.R: People shouted at them, "Get away! You are unclean! Get away! Get away! Do not touch us!" \q So they ran off and wandered from place to place. \q People in other nations said, "They cannot live here with us."

fr.L: « Écartez-vous ! Impur ! » leur criait-on ; « Écartez-vous ! Écartez-vous ! Ne touchez pas ! » \q Car ils ont fui et aussi erré ; \q on a dit parmi les nations : « Ils ne continueront pas à séjourner [ici]. »
fr.B: « Allez-vous-en ! Impurs ! » leur criait-on. « Allez-vous-en ! Allez-vous-en ! Ne nous touchez pas ! » \q Alors ils se sont enfuis et ont erré d’un lieu à l’autre, \q et parmi les nations on disait : « Ils ne peuvent plus rester ici. »
fr.R: Les gens leur criaient : « Allez-vous-en ! Vous êtes impurs ! Allez-vous-en ! Allez-vous-en ! Ne nous touchez pas ! » \q Alors ils se sont enfuis et ont erré d’un endroit à l’autre. \q Dans les autres nations, les gens disaient : « Ils ne peuvent pas vivre ici avec nous. »

decisions.choice: Unclean!: the cry that warned others away
decisions.reason: A person with a skin disease had to cry out "Unclean, unclean!" so that others would keep away (Leviticus 13:45-46). Here others shout it at the defiled prophets and priests, treating them as outcasts.

decisions.choice: for they fled and wandered: so they became homeless
decisions.reason: The word "for" (ki) links the shouting to its result: driven off, they became fugitives and wanderers, like Cain (Genesis 4:12, 14). The verb "fled" is rare and its sense is not quite certain.

decisions.choice: they will not continue to sojourn: they may not stay as guests
decisions.reason: To sojourn (gur) is to live in a place as an outsider under its people's protection. Even among other nations no one would let them stay.

decisions.choice: Do not touch us! (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "us", who the cry is meant to protect.

source.text: פְּנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ חִלְּקָ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַבִּיטָ֑ם פְּנֵ֤י כֹהֲנִים֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔אוּ וּזְקֵנִ֖יםלֹ֥א חָנָֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] face of Yahweh has divided them; not he will continue to look on them; [the] face of priests not they lifted, and elders not they favored.

en.L: The face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has scattered them; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will look on them no more; \q they did not lift up the face of priests, and they showed no favor to elders.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s own presence has scattered them; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will no longer look on them with care. \q No respect was shown to the priests, no kindness to the elders.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has scattered them. He will not care for them anymore. \q No one respected the priests or was kind to the elders.

fr.L: La face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} les a dispersés ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne les regardera plus ; \q ils n’ont pas relevé la face des prêtres, et ils n’ont pas fait grâce aux anciens.
fr.B: La présence même {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} les a dispersés ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne veillera plus sur eux avec bienveillance. \q On n’a montré aucun respect aux prêtres, aucune bonté aux anciens.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} les a dispersés. Il ne prendra plus soin d’eux. \q Personne n’a respecté les prêtres ni n’a été bon avec les anciens.

decisions.choice: pe before ayin
decisions.reason: Verse 16 begins with the letter pe and verse 17 with ayin, the reverse of the order in chapter 1, as in 2:16-17 and 3:46-51 (see the note at 2:1).

decisions.choice: the face of the LORD has scattered them: the LORD in person, turned against them
decisions.reason: The LORD's face is his presence, here turned against them in judgment (Psalm 34:17; Leviticus 17:10); he himself has scattered them among the nations. "To look on" someone is to regard them with care (Psalm 13:4; Isaiah 66:2).

decisions.choice: they did not lift up the face of priests: they showed priests no honor
decisions.reason: To lift someone's face is to honor them or show them favor (Genesis 19:21; Deuteronomy 28:50, where the conquering nation "will not lift up the face of the old"). "They" are most likely the enemy; it could be the people. Compare 5:12.

decisions.choice: and elders, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) has "and" before "elders"; the written consonants (ketiv) have the word without it. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the LORD's own presence (B); the LORD himself (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the face of the LORD" means here.

source.text: עוֹדֵ֨ינוּ֙ תִּכְלֶ֣ינָה עֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֶל־עֶזְרָתֵ֖נוּ הָ֑בֶל בְּצִפִּיָּתֵ֣נוּ צִפִּ֔ינוּ אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Still our eyes failed [looking] for our help, [in] vain; in our watching we watched for a nation [that] would not save.

en.L: Still our eyes failed, [looking] for our help, in vain; \q in our watching we watched for a nation that could not save.
en.B: Our eyes still strained, looking for help that came to nothing; \q from our watchtower we watched for a nation that could not save us.
en.R: We kept looking for someone to help us until our eyes were worn out, but it was no use. \q From our watchtowers we watched for a nation to rescue us, but it could not.

fr.L: Encore nos yeux se consumaient [à attendre] notre secours, en vain ; \q dans notre guet, nous avons guetté une nation qui ne pouvait pas sauver.
fr.B: Nos yeux s’épuisaient encore à attendre un secours qui n’est jamais venu ; \q du haut de notre tour de guet, nous avons guetté une nation qui ne pouvait pas nous sauver.
fr.R: Nous avons cherché quelqu’un pour nous aider jusqu’à en avoir les yeux usés, mais c’était inutile. \q Du haut de nos tours de guet, nous attendions une nation qui viendrait nous sauver, mais elle ne le pouvait pas.

decisions.choice: our: the poet speaks with the people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 20 the poet says "we", speaking with the people who lived through the siege. The reading the scribes marked (qere) has "still we"; the written consonants (ketiv) have a form that may be read "still they" (still they failed, our eyes). The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: our eyes failed: worn out with looking and waiting
decisions.reason: Eyes "fail" when they are worn out by weeping or by long waiting for something that does not come (2:11; Psalm 69:4; Jeremiah 14:6).

decisions.choice: a nation that could not save: Egypt
decisions.reason: During the siege Judah hoped for help from Egypt. An Egyptian army came out, and the Babylonians withdrew for a time, but the Egyptians went home and the siege resumed (Jeremiah 37:5-10; compare Isaiah 30:1-7). The word for watching may name a watchtower or the act of keeping watch.

decisions.choice: from our watchtower
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the noun as the place of watching.

source.text: צָד֣וּ צְעָדֵ֔ינוּ מִלֶּ֖כֶת בִּרְחֹבֹתֵ֑ינוּ קָרַ֥ב קִצֵּ֛ינוּ מָלְא֥וּ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כִּי־בָ֥א קִצֵּֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They hunted our steps from walking in our squares; drew near our end, were full our days, for had come our end.

en.L: They hunted our steps, from walking in our squares; \q our end drew near; our days were fulfilled, for our end had come.
en.B: They tracked our steps so we could not walk in our own squares; \q our end drew near, our days were over, for our end had come.
en.R: Our enemies watched every move we made, so we could not walk in our city squares. \q Our end was near. Our time was up. Our end had come.

fr.L: Ils ont traqué nos pas, [nous empêchant] de marcher sur nos places ; \q notre fin s’est approchée ; nos jours se sont accomplis, car notre fin était venue.
fr.B: Ils épiaient nos pas, si bien que nous ne pouvions plus marcher sur nos propres places ; \q notre fin approchait, nos jours étaient finis, car notre fin était arrivée.
fr.R: Nos ennemis surveillaient chacun de nos mouvements, et nous ne pouvions plus marcher sur les places de notre ville. \q Notre fin était proche. Notre temps était fini. Notre fin était arrivée.

decisions.choice: they hunted our steps: enemies watched every movement
decisions.reason: The besiegers built siege walls and towers around the city (2 Kings 25:1; Jeremiah 52:4) and could watch and shoot at anyone in the open squares. "From walking" means "so that we could not walk".

decisions.choice: our end has come
decisions.reason: The words recall the prophets' warnings: "the end has come upon my people Israel" (Amos 8:2; Ezekiel 7:2-6). What was threatened has happened.

decisions.choice: Our enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

source.text: קַלִּ֤ים הָיוּ֙ רֹדְפֵ֔ינוּ מִנִּשְׁרֵ֖י שָׁמָ֑יִם עַל־הֶהָרִ֣ים דְּלָקֻ֔נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר אָ֥רְבוּ לָֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Swift were our pursuers more than [the] eagles of [the] heavens; on the mountains they chased us; in the wilderness they lay in wait for us.

en.L: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the heavens; \q on the mountains they hotly pursued us; in the wilderness they lay in wait for us.
en.B: Those who hunted us were quicker than eagles in the sky; \q they chased us over the mountains, they set ambushes for us in the wilderness.
en.R: The enemies who chased us were faster than eagles flying in the sky. \q They chased us across the mountains and hid in the desert to catch us.

fr.L: Nos poursuivants ont été plus rapides que les aigles des cieux ; \q sur les montagnes ils nous ont pourchassés ; dans le désert ils nous ont tendu des embuscades.
fr.B: Ceux qui nous pourchassaient étaient plus rapides que les aigles du ciel ; \q ils nous ont poursuivis sur les montagnes, ils nous ont dressé des embuscades dans le désert.
fr.R: Les ennemis qui nous poursuivaient étaient plus rapides que des aigles qui volent dans le ciel. \q Ils nous ont pourchassés à travers les montagnes et se sont cachés dans le désert pour nous attraper.

decisions.choice: swifter than eagles: the swift enemy of the covenant warnings
decisions.reason: The law warned that God would bring a nation "as swift as the eagle flies" against a disobedient people (Deuteronomy 28:49), and Jeremiah said the same of the invader from the north (Jeremiah 4:13). The bird (nesher) may be the eagle or the griffon vulture.

decisions.choice: in the wilderness they lay in wait: the flight from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: When the wall was breached, King Zedekiah and his soldiers fled toward the Arabah, the desert valley of the Jordan, and were caught near Jericho (2 Kings 25:4-5). The verse leads into verse 20.

decisions.choice: they hotly pursued us: they chased us closely
decisions.reason: The verb (dalaq) means to burn, and from that to chase in hot pursuit (Genesis 31:36).

source.text: ר֤וּחַ אַפֵּ֨ינוּ֙ מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה נִלְכַּ֖ד בִּשְׁחִיתוֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְנוּ בְּצִלּ֖וֹ נִֽחְיֶ֥ה בַגּוֹיִֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] breath of our nostrils, [the] anointed of Yahweh, was captured in their pits, [he] of whom we said, In his shadow we will live among the nations.

en.L: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, was captured in their pits, \q [he] of whom we said, "In his shadow we will live among the nations."
en.B: The very breath of our life, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed, was caught in their traps, \q the one of whom we had said, "Under his protection we will live among the nations."
en.R: Our king, whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had anointed, was as precious to us as the breath of life. But he was caught in their traps. \q We had said, "He will protect us, and we will live safely among the nations."

fr.L: Le souffle de nos narines, l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, a été pris dans leurs fosses, \q [lui] dont nous disions : « À son ombre nous vivrons parmi les nations. »
fr.B: Le souffle même de notre vie, l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, a été pris dans leurs pièges, \q lui dont nous avions dit : « Sous sa protection, nous vivrons parmi les nations. »
fr.R: Notre roi, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait oint, nous était aussi précieux que le souffle de la vie. Mais il a été pris dans leurs pièges. \q Nous avions dit : « Il nous protégera, et nous vivrons en sécurité parmi les nations. »

decisions.choice: the LORD's anointed was captured: King Zedekiah
decisions.reason: "The LORD's anointed" is the king of David's line (1 Samuel 24:7; Psalm 89:39). Jerusalem's last king, Zedekiah, fled the city by night and was captured near Jericho; the Babylonians killed his sons before his eyes, blinded him and took him to Babylon (2 Kings 25:4-7; Jeremiah 39:4-7).

decisions.choice: the breath of our nostrils: the one our life depended on
decisions.reason: Breath is life itself (Genesis 2:7). The king was the people's life, the one on whom their survival seemed to rest.

decisions.choice: their pits: hunters' traps
decisions.reason: Hunters dug pits to catch animals (Psalm 35:7; Jeremiah 18:22). Ezekiel pictures the kings of Judah as young lions caught in a pit and led away (Ezekiel 19:4, 8).

decisions.choice: in his shadow: under his protection
decisions.reason: Shade is protection from the burning sun, and so a picture of a ruler's protection (Judges 9:15; Isaiah 30:2; 32:2). The people had hoped to live safely under their king even among hostile nations.

decisions.choice: Our king, whom the LORD had anointed
decisions.reason: Readable says that the anointed one is the king.

decisions.choice: under his protection
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the shade stands for.

decisions.choice: "l’oint du SEIGNEUR", lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span on "lui", "son", "il"
decisions.reason: The anointed one here is the king of Judah (m1), not God, so his pronouns are ordinary French, as the English has no span on them.

source.text: שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ע֑וּץ גַּם־עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ תַּעֲבָר־כּ֔וֹס תִּשְׁכְּרִ֖י וְתִתְעָרִֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, dwelling in [the] land of Uz; also to you will pass [the] cup; you will become drunk and make yourself naked.

en.L: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz; \q to you also the cup will pass; you will become drunk and strip yourself naked.
en.B: Rejoice and be glad, Daughter Edom, you who live in the land of Uz! \q But the cup will be passed to you as well; you will get drunk and strip yourself bare.
en.R: People of Edom, who live in the land of Uz, go ahead and celebrate now! \q But you too will have to drink from the cup of God's anger. You will get drunk and lie naked in shame.

fr.L: Réjouis-toi et sois dans l’allégresse, fille d’Édom, toi qui habites au pays d’Outs ; \q à toi aussi la coupe passera ; tu t’enivreras et tu te mettras à nu.
fr.B: Réjouis-toi, sois dans la joie, fille d’Édom, toi qui habites au pays d’Outs ! \q Mais la coupe te sera passée à toi aussi ; tu t’enivreras et tu te dénuderas.
fr.R: Peuple d’Édom, toi qui habites au pays d’Outs, vas-y, fais la fête maintenant ! \q Mais toi aussi, tu devras boire la coupe de la colère de Dieu. Tu seras ivre et tu te retrouveras nu, couvert de honte.

decisions.choice: rejoice and be glad: said in bitter irony
decisions.reason: Edom rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall and joined in plundering it (Psalm 137:7; Obadiah 10-14; Ezekiel 35:15). The command is mocking: let Edom enjoy it while it can, for its turn is coming.

decisions.choice: daughter of Edom ... the land of Uz: the people of Edom
decisions.reason: "Daughter Edom" pictures the nation as a woman, as "daughter Zion" does. Uz was a region east or southeast of Judah linked with Edom (Genesis 36:28; Jeremiah 25:20; Job 1:1). The reading the scribes marked (qere) has the usual form "who dwells"; the written consonants (ketiv) have an older form with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: the cup will pass to you: Edom too will drink God's anger
decisions.reason: The cup is the cup of the LORD's wrath, which makes the nations reel like drunkards (Jeremiah 25:15-29, where Edom and Uz are both named; 49:12; Isaiah 51:17). Drunkenness and nakedness picture helpless shame (Genesis 9:21; Habakkuk 2:15-16).

decisions.choice: the cup of God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup is (m3).

decisions.choice: "le pays d’Outs"
decisions.reason: The form of the name already published in Genesis 10:23, 1 Chronicles 1:17 and Jeremiah 25:20.

source.text: תַּם־עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַגְלוֹתֵ֑ךְ פָּקַ֤ד עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־אֱד֔וֹם גִּלָּ֖ה עַל־חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Is finished your iniquity, daughter of Zion; not he will continue to exile you; he will punish your iniquity, daughter of Edom; he will uncover your sins.

en.L: Your iniquity is finished, daughter of Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not continue to exile you; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish your iniquity, daughter of Edom; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will uncover your sins.
en.B: Your punishment is complete, Daughter Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not keep you in exile any longer. \q But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish your guilt, Daughter Edom; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will expose your sins.
en.R: People of Zion, your punishment is over. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not keep you in exile any longer. \q But people of Edom, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will punish you for your sin. He will show everyone your sins.

fr.L: Ta faute est achevée, fille de Sion ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne continuera pas à t’exiler ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} punira ta faute, fille d’Édom ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mettra à nu tes péchés.
fr.B: Ta punition est accomplie, fille de Sion ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne te gardera plus en exil. \q Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} punira ta faute, fille d’Édom ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dévoilera tes péchés.
fr.R: Peuple de Sion, ta punition est terminée. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne te gardera plus en exil. \q Mais peuple d’Édom, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te punira pour ton péché. Il montrera à tous tes péchés.

decisions.choice: your iniquity is finished: your punishment is complete
decisions.reason: The word ('awon) can mean a wrong or the punishment it brings (see verse 6). Said to Zion, with the end of exile, it means the punishment has run its course (compare Isaiah 40:2). Said to Edom, the same word is the guilt for which Edom will now be punished.

decisions.choice: he will not continue to exile you: your exile will not go on
alternatives: he will not exile you again
decisions.reason: "He" is the LORD, unnamed here. The phrase may mean that he will not prolong Zion's exile, or that he will never exile her again; both promise that the judgment is at an end.

decisions.choice: he will uncover your sins: Edom's guilt will be exposed
decisions.reason: The verb for uncovering (galah) is the same one used for sending into exile in the line before. Zion's exile ends; Edom's sins are laid bare, as one is stripped naked (verse 21).

decisions.choice: punishment (Zion); guilt (B), sin (R) (Edom)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in m1 for each use of 'awon; Literal keeps "iniquity" both times. Verse 6 explains the choice of "punishment".

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD, the unnamed "he" of both lines (m2).
